newsitem.title: POLAND: Court jails Pole who sent 54 girls to prostitution.
newsitem.headline: Court jails Pole who sent 54 girls to prostitution.

text.p: A Polish court on Monday jailed a man for seven years for sending young women to work in brothels in Germany and Switzerland between 1992 and 1995, PAP news agency reported.
The agency said the provincial court in the northwestern port city Szczecin also fined the 32-year-old Pole, identified only as Wlodzimierz R.
Another Pole, aged 20, was given a year in jail for helping him.

The case has further highlighted the plight of many Polish girls, lured to western Europe with promises of work, either as prostitutes or in such jobs as waitressing, who end up suffering brutality and exploitation in western brothels.

The indictment said the defendant had sent 54 local women abroad, 43 of whom had known they were going to work as prostitutes but 11 of whom were told they would be home-helps, cleaners or grape pickers.
He was also accused of living off immoral earnings because of escort agencies he ran in Poland, but he was acquitted of rape charges, PAP said.
